title: regional-mesh-fallback-latency-smoothing-playbook-draft
body:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook sketch for orchestrating a graceful regional mesh fallback with traffic smoothing to reduce tail-latency and cache thrash during cross-region diversion. It consolidates operator heuristics, a lightweight automation recipe, and short lab notes from our Feb 2025 simulations.

When to use this playbook (scenarios):
- Partial region egress degradation (packet loss, peering flap) causing elevated p95/p99 for region-local requests.
- Regional control-plane degradation where routing decisions are unreliable but compute still available.
- Unexpected capacity drop in a region (node eviction, infra maintenance) where immediate full cutover would cause cache cold-start cascades.

Goals:
1) Keep global SLOs for successful responses while minimizing request-level tail-latency spikes.
2) Avoid kvcache and prefix-cache blowout by doing staged weight moves and warm priming.
3) Provide clear operator decision thresholds and safe rollback paths.

High-level strategy:
1) Detect -> Verify -> Prime -> Smooth shift -> Monitor -> Conclude (and document)

Detection signals (primary):
- region.*.egress_loss > 2% sustained for 3m OR region.*.peer_rtt_spike > 250ms for 2m
- region.*.p95_api_latency > baseline_by_2x AND region.*.error_rate_increase > 0.5%
- CDN or edge provider alerts mapped to region tag

Verification checklist (operator):
- Confirm alert context in Ops Slack channel #sre-regional-alerts. Paste top 3 metrics (p50/p95/error-rate) and region hash.
- Run quick reachability checks: curl -I from other regions -> check server response codes.
- Check control-plane health: api-controlplane-<region> latency and leader-election logs.
- Validate that Dedicated customer capacity limits are not being exceeded before moving traffic.

Priming (warm standby) steps:
- If fallback target region is warm-standby, ensure kvcache preseed is enabled for critical prefixes. Use preseed job:
  ./ops/preseed-kvcache --from region=<source> --to region=<target> --prefixes=common-prompts,session-keys --concurrency=8
- Kick a small synthetic fanout from source region to target region (5 RPS synthetic per zone) for 5 minutes to warm JIT caches and populate KV caches. Tag these traffic jobs with run_id and keep logs.
- For models with long initial generation costs (long-context configs), run 3 warm startup traces for 2k tokens to prime kv/hw paths.

Smoothing parameters (recommended defaults):
- step_percent = 15% (do not move more than 15% of total ingress per operator step)
- grace_seconds = 120 (allow 2m to observe effects at each step)
- smooth_window = 5m (rolling window to compute p95/p99 deltas)
- cooldown_between_steps = 4m (includes grace_seconds)
- max_steps = 6 (cap at 90%)

Operator flow:
1) Announce plan in #sre-regional-alerts and @oncall. Post: planned smoothing handoff from <affected-region> -> <fallback-region>, starting at T+5m, steps=15%/step, max=90%.
2) Ensure preseed job succeeded (exit code 0 and item_count > 1k for most prefixes).
3) Execute first weight change using traffic-control CLI:
  trafficctl shift-weights --from <affected-region> --to <fallback-region> --percent 15 --dry-run=false --run-id=<YYYYMMDD>-mesh-fallback
4) Watch primary dashboards for the smooth_window: p50/p95/p99, error_rate, kvcache_hit_ratio, egress_saturation, cpu_steal.
5) If any of the following occur during grace_seconds or smooth_window, abort and roll back the last step immediately:
   - p99 increases > 30% above baseline AND error_rate increases > 0.3%
   - kvcache_hit_ratio drops > 10% absolute points
   - host_cpu > 90% on fallback-region nodes sustained for > 1m
6) If metrics look stable, wait cooldown_between_steps and repeat.

Abort and rollback procedure:
- Immediate rollback command:
  trafficctl rollback --run-id=<run-id> --to-original=true --grace=60
- Notify product/SRE chat with rollback reason and attach metric screenshots.
- If rollback fails (trafficctl error or API timeout), trigger DNS TTL mitigation (see DNS section) and involve platform-engineering channel.

DNS considerations (when to touch DNS):
- Prefer not to change DNS for short window fallbacks. Use traffic-control and edge weight reports.
- If routing plane shows asymmetric reachability and we need client-side redirection (e.g., customer on long DNS TTLs), coordinate TTL reduce via:
  dnsctl set-ttl example-cname 60 --region=global --note="SRE mesh fallback TTL reduction"
- Always allow 5–10 minutes after TTL change to propagate before relying on client DNS behavior.

Edge and networking notes:
- Avoid global BGP-level announcements for quick shifts; they introduce flaps. Prefer overlay weight changes at our edge/proxy layer.
- If upstream ISP outage requires BGP reannouncement, coordinate with netops and set a 10m maintenance window.

Metrics to watch (dashboards):
- global/requests: p50/p95/p99 by region and by route
- region/<r>/kv_cache: hit_ratio, eviction_rate, load
- region/<r>/egress: loss_rate, retransmits, peer_rtt
- infra/<r>/cpu_util, infra/<r>/gmem_pressure, infra/<r>/loadavg
- client-facing/error_types: 5xx_by_route, 429_by_route

Smoke tests after each step:
- run smoke suite (sre-smoke) limited to 10 routes:
  ./sre-smoke --routes quick-chat,embeddings,model-status --concurrency=20 --target-region=<fallback-region>
- Validate: 95% of smoke requests < 2x baseline latency, no new 5xx errors in smoke logs.

Lab notes (Feb 2025 simulation, summary):
- Scenario: simulated 20% packet loss on us-west egress for 6 minutes.
- Findings:
  - Full immediate 100% cutover produced 3x p99 spike in eu-central for models with large KV windows (cache cold-start).
  - Staged 15% steps with priming kept p99 within 1.3x baseline and error rate increase <0.2%.
  - Excessive short-step cadence (<90s) caused oscillation between edge caches; recommended cooldown_between_steps >= 4m.
  - Preseeding KV caches reduced cold-start cost by ~45% (measured token generation time).

Operator playbook examples (cheat-sheet):
- Quick status: runops status --scope=region:us-west --metrics=p95,p99,errors,kvcache
- Start priming: ops/preseed-kvcache --from=us-west --to=eu-central --prefixes=default,usersessions --concurrency=6
- Shift 15%: trafficctl shift-weights --from=us-west --to=eu-central --percent=15 --run-id=20250304-meshtest
- Rollback last: trafficctl rollback --run-id=20250304-meshtest --to-original=true

Open questions and TODOs:
- Should we add dynamic step sizing based on current load (e.g., percent = min(15, 10% * overload_factor))? Needs a small R&D spike. Owner: Marcus Lee.
- Improve preseed visibility: add metrics for preseed success per-prefix. Owner: Priya Shah.
- Automate smoke-run validation and auto-abort if smoke failures exceed threshold. Owner: Jonas Muller.
- Formalize TTL change approval workflow for customer-impacting DNS changes. Owner: Ana Gomez.

Post-incident doc template (fill after any use):
- Incident start/end times
- Trigger signals
- Actions taken (priming, steps, rollbacks) with timestamps and run-ids
- Metric deltas (p50/p95/p99, errors, kvcache hit) pre/during/post
- Lessons learned and owners for follow-up actions

Appendix: Useful commands and links
- trafficctl docs: https://internal.redwood/trafficctl/docs
- kv preseed script: https://internal.redwood/ops/preseed-kvcache
- smoke test runner: https://internal.redwood/sre-smoke

Footnotes:
- This is an iterative draft. Keep notes here for the next oncall rotation. When we converge on defaults, migrate to Confluence and codify automation in traffic-control repo.

Recent edits:
- 2025-02-10: initial draft (Evelyn)
- 2025-02-18: added lab results and smoothing params (Marcus)
- 2025-03-04: clarified kvcache preseed commands and open-action owners (Priya)
